## About

Japanese-market OM-5 Mark II bodies show their menus in Japanese. This research found that the official 1.1 update already contains the English text, and builds a replacement for the language component only (component 0101). The Japanese language slot is pointed at an English-based table, keeping the original Japanese font. No program code and no region setting is changed.

English has no text for 39 messages the Japanese firmware shows; the researchers wrote their own translations for those, which are not official. The table fits within the firmware's own string buffer, though that does not prove every line fits every screen.

The repository holds Python code, tests and exact hashes to rebuild the file offline from your own copy of the stock 1.1 update, and no firmware. The research was carried out with AI agents and the camera steps by the owner. It is experimental; even a resource-only update erases and rewrites a 12 MiB range, and recovery after a damaged resource is unknown.

## Research notes

One owner reports a normal boot and English menus on a Japanese-market OM-5 Mark II on official 1.1 after installing the resource-only r01 on 26 November 2026, with only partial follow-up checks. The repository reproduces the bytes offline from a separately supplied stock file whose digest matches the Atlas's 1.1 record. Full UI coverage, long-term reliability and recovery after a damaged resource are unverified. Native E148 only; it makes no claim for the original OM-5 (E144) or ports.
